title: Affine torsion cohomology vanishes above the transcendence-degree support bound
statement: Let $L$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], let $T$ be an affine scheme of finite type over $L$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-scheme], and let $G$ be a torsion abelian etale sheaf on $T$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. Let $c\geq0$ be an integer and assume that every point $t$ in the support of $G$ [def-kun-support] satisfies $\operatorname{trdeg}_L\kappa(t)\leq c$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then $H^r(T_{\mathrm{et}},G)=0$ for every integer $r>c$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 0F0W, lemma-interlude-II, separably closed base-field case (cd(L)=0)

proof.text: By the definition of support, the hypothesis says that every geometric stalk of $G$ above a point of transcendence degree greater than $c$ is zero. Apply [lem-sc-support-dimension-union] to $B=T$, $K=L$, $N=G$, $a=c$. Thus $G=\varinjlim_Z G_Z$, where $Z$ ranges over the closed subsets of $T$ of dimension at most $c$ and $G_Z=\ker(G\to j_{Z*}j_Z^{-1}G)$. This is a small directed system: closed subsets form a set, the empty subset is included, and finite unions remain closed of dimension at most $c$ (each irreducible closed subset of a finite union lies in one member).

source.place: Tag 0F0W, lemma-interlude-II, first sentence; support approximation Tag 0F0N, lemma-support-in-subset

proof.text: By [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel], the kernel inclusion is sectionwise injective. Each $G_Z$ is torsion: its sections inject into those of $G$, so any local integer annihilating a section of $G$ annihilates the corresponding section of $G_Z$. For an etale object $V\to T$ factoring through $T\setminus Z$, the map $G(V)\to(j_{Z*}j_Z^{-1}G)(V)$ is the identity under restriction, hence $G_Z(V)=0$. Every geometric point outside $Z$ has such neighbourhoods, so $G_Z$ has zero stalk there. Realize $Z$ as the image of a closed immersion $i_Z:W_Z\to T$. By [lem-kun-04ca], $G_Z\cong i_{Z*}M_Z$ with $M_Z=i_Z^{-1}G_Z$. This inverse image is torsion: for each geometric point $\bar w$ of $W_Z$, [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] identifies $(i_Z^{-1}G_Z)_{\bar w}$ with $(G_Z)_{i_Z\bar w}$. The latter is a torsion group by the stalk characterization in [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations], applied to the torsion sheaf $G_Z$; applying that characterization on $W_Z$ proves that $M_Z$ is torsion.

source.place: Tag 0F0W, lemma-interlude-II, omitted details: supported sheaves via Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward; inverse-image stalk formula Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (3)

proof.text: By the locally-finite-type affine-pairs criterion and the finite-type hypothesis, write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a finitely generated $L$-algebra. The affine characterization of a closed immersion gives $W_Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_Z)$. Images in $A/I_Z$ of finitely many $L$-algebra generators of $A$ still generate the quotient, so $W_Z$ is affine and finite type over $L$. The homeomorphism of $W_Z$ with $Z$ identifies chains of irreducible closed subsets, giving $\dim W_Z=\dim Z\leq c$. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $T$, the same closed-immersion characterization gives $i_Z^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J_U)$ for an ideal $J_U$. This quotient is generated by $1$ as an $R$-module. Thus $i_Z$ is affine and its ring map over every affine open is finite, exactly the definition of a finite morphism.

source.place: Tag 0F0W, lemma-interlude-II, omitted details: closed subschemes of the affine finite-type scheme

proof.text: The separably closed point lemma gives $\kuncd(\operatorname{Spec}L)=0$. The definitions [def-kun-cd] and [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] quantify over the same torsion abelian sheaves and ordinary etale cohomology, so $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(L)\leq0$. Apply [thm-sc-affine-torsion-cd] to the affine finite-type scheme $W_Z$: for nonempty $W_Z$, $H^r(W_{Z,\mathrm{et}},M_Z)=0$ for $r>\dim W_Z$, hence for $r>c$. If $W_Z$ is empty, every object of its small etale site is empty; the empty covering forces its sections to be the zero group by the sheaf axiom. Its abelian-sheaf category therefore has only the zero object, so derived sections and all cohomology groups are zero. Since $i_Z$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology] identifies $H^r(T_{\mathrm{et}},G_Z)$ with $H^r(W_{Z,\mathrm{et}},M_Z)$, so the former group is zero for $r>c$.

source.place: Tag 0F0W, lemma-interlude-II, affine bound Tag 0F0V, proposition-cd-affine, and finite-pushforward/Leray comparison Tag 03QP

proof.text: The affine scheme $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] to the directed system $G_Z$. For $r>c\geq0$, all stage groups are zero by step 4, so $H^r(T_{\mathrm{et}},G)\cong\varinjlim_Z H^r(T_{\mathrm{et}},G_Z)=0$. The assertion includes $G=0$, $T$ empty, $c=0$, and nonreduced $T$; none of the preceding arguments requires reducedness or an exponent annihilating all of $G$.

source.place: Tag 0F0W, lemma-interlude-II, final sentence; Tag 03Q5, lemma-colimit
